surfaceDriftSincePin.head: 4762e9e0
surfaceDriftSincePin.note: Commit counts are a WHERE-TO-LOOK signal, not a verdict — a commit can touch a surface without moving a pixel. The one row measured properly (BL-0169 brand-pro-mode, recaptured on the seed fixture) differs by 45.67% of pixels. media and insert are the only surfaces untouched since the pin.
surfaceDriftSincePin.floorExplained: Six panel roots landed in a 12.6-14.6% band, media included, and media has zero commits since the pin. Read side by side, the Media panel body is unchanged — the band is the SHELL every editor frame contains. ReviewBar (869cebb2, 2026-08-17, board 200:213) added a whole row under the topbar whenever a round is open, and the seed fixture has one; the inspector is present in the new renders and absent in the old. Vertical re-alignment does not cancel it (best offset is 0), because a new row is not a translation. CONSEQUENCE for the per-row path: the panel-level signal is real and usable — 45.67% on Brand vs a flat floor on Media is exactly the discrimination it was built for — but every editor frame's chrome is stale regardless of its panel, so 'redraw only what moved' still touches the shell band of all 48. Founder call: redraw all 48, or redraw the shell band once if the frames are componentised enough to swap it.
surfaceDriftSincePin.panelRegionMethod: drift-diff.mjs --region 60,56,320,844 confines the comparison to the left drawer and searches +-64px of vertical alignment. It settles on dy=48px by itself — the ReviewBar's own height — which is the shell offset cancelled. Calibrated: media 2.13% (zero commits since the pin, panel confirmed identical by eye), layers 4.23% (the eye/lock icons were recoloured), brand 15.70% (tabs became a drill-in list). Read >~8% as 'the panel moved'.

panelDrift._threshold: >~8% = the panel moved; below = keep the frame (calibrated on media 2.13%, zero commits since the pin, confirmed identical by eye)

surfaceDriftSincePin.shellBandNote: FOUNDER CALL 2026-08-18: redraw a frame only when its PANEL moved; the shell band in every editor frame stays as drawn and is known-stale — it predates ReviewBar (869cebb2, 2026-08-17). Componentising the shell was considered and declined for now: the frames hold zero components (433 raw frames each), so there is nothing to swap without building it first.

surfaceDriftSincePin.specsMustAssertTheState: A capture spec whose actions do not END in a waitFor on something the state proves will happily screenshot the state it failed to open, and the diff then reports a plausible number. Caught here: comments-open and review-pill-open both read exactly 10.86%, which is the shell region and nothing else — adding waitFor on [role=menu],[role=dialog],[role=listbox] turned both into honest FAILs while the other four still passed.
surfaceDriftSincePin.capturesLeakThroughLocalStorage: capture.mjs runs every screen in ONE browser context, and the editor remembers its open panel in localStorage. So screen N's destination is still open when screen N+1 loads: an 'Export code' capture came back showing Version History because the previous row had opened it. Normalise at the top of each spec's actions (click a known rail tab first) or the batch quietly measures the wrong screens — the first sitemenu run produced three PAIRS of identical percentages and two byte-identical PNGs.
surfaceDriftSincePin.correction: An earlier version of this table said media 0 and insert 0, and a commit message repeated that they were 'the only surfaces untouched since the pin'. Both were wrong. The media count was taken with two paths in one unquoted shell variable and came back 0 instead of 37; the insert count was 0 because the path it named does not exist (the tab is sidebar/tabs/elements + ElementsTab.tsx, not sidebar/tabs/insert). No editor surface is untouched since the pin. This is exactly why the founder's per-row pixel measure is the authority and the counts are only a where-to-look hint: BL-0103, the media panel ROOT, measures 2.13%% and is identical by eye, while BL-0161, the media FULL-PAGE library on the same 37-commit surface, measures 40.73%% and was rebuilt outright — 'Media library EXPANDED' with Stock/Compact became 'Asset Library MANAGE' with a folders sidebar and Import URL. One commit count cannot tell those two apart. The pixels can.
surfaceDriftSincePin.doorsThatMoved: Brand's rows were renamed since the pin and the old row names are dead ends for a capture spec: BL-0173 'brand-styles-tab' is now the row labelled **Presets** (id still `styles`), and BL-0170 'brand-dark-preview' is now **Colour mode**. Four site-menu rows lost their labels entirely — site-settings, version-history, components, keyboard-shortcuts. A row that cannot be captured is not necessarily a broken product; usually its door was renamed.
surfaceDriftSincePin.regionMustMatchTheState: BL-0175 measured 92.30%% against the drawer region and 26.14%% against the modal region. Both numbers are real: the old shot dims the drawer behind an open modal and the new one does not, so the drawer region was measuring a backdrop. Measure a modal row in the modal.
surfaceDriftSincePin.offRailDoorsAreByDesign: Settings, Version History, Components, Publish and History have no rail icon: the rail is six items by board 52:2, and LeftSidebar says off-rail panels open from ⌘K, shortcuts and the topbar (guarded by tabsConfig.figma.test.ts). Checked before calling anything stranded — pressing S really does open Settings. So the inventory rows named 'sitemenu-site-settings' and 'sitemenu-version-history' are still capturable, just not from the site menu: S, H, ⇧A, U reach them.
surfaceDriftSincePin.knownResiduals: Two things a DOM measure cannot reach, both small and both recorded rather than faked: unit suffixes in the inspector ('px' after a number) are CSS ::after content and have no node to read; and Figma renders Inter a shade wider than Chrome, so a line of wrapped copy can break one word earlier or later. Text alignment WAS missing for the first inspector frame (labels are right-aligned in the app, left in BL-0129) and is captured from BL-0124 on.
surfaceDriftSincePin.correctionSiteMenu: An earlier note here said site-settings, version-history, components and keyboard-shortcuts were 'no longer labels in the site menu'. They are all there — the claim came from a regex over SiteMenu.tsx that only matched a subset of the markup. Measuring the open menu listed nineteen items across five groups, including all four.
surfaceDriftSincePin.overlayMeasureNotes: Overlays needed three fixes before they measured at all. The walk stopped descending at a zero-size box, and a portal root has no size — every popover came back as two nodes. It also stopped descending when a node fell outside the region, but an absolutely-positioned child escapes its parent: the site menu hangs off the 32x32 topbar button, nowhere near the region the menu occupies. And a region-only walk picked up the page BEHIND the overlay, so specs now name a `root` selector and the walk starts there.
surfaceDriftSincePin.measureRespectsAncestorOpacity: Opacity does not inherit as a computed value, so a child of a faded ancestor still reports opacity 1. Until the walk checked ancestors, a CLOSED panel measured as a full screen of content — 50 nodes with real geometry for a surface at opacity 0. The walk climbs now.

driftRegions._note: Whole-frame comparison does not work: the alignment search picks dy=0 because the topbar never moved and the canvas content dominates, so the ReviewBar offset below it is never cancelled. Each state family needs the band its state actually lives in. Rail is 0-60, drawer 60-380, canvas 380-1140, inspector 1140-1440; the shell above starts at 56.

driftSweepProgress.note: Each remaining row needs its capture spec rebuilt by hand — the originals were never committed (only screens-auth.json was). Reaching a state is the slow part: BL-0159's stock browser took three attempts because the entry moved into the panel footer as 'Browse stock' and even that lands on a source picker. Log in as the seed fixture's owner (qa@buildrik.local), not your own user, or /edit redirects and the failure reads as a sentinel timeout.
driftSweepProgress.remainingRows: BL-0162 (fixture has no media, so the list toggle is disabled — adding an asset would restate every verified Media row) · BL-0172 (NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_DS_AI unset, so there is no state to capture)
driftSweepProgress.redrawCost: BL-0105, the first: 1 clean recapture (the rail tooltip was covering a row in the first reference), 1 computed-style measuring probe, 5 use_figma calls (structure / rows / footer / icons / icon size), 3 screenshots to check. The subtree is 260 nodes; building it as data-driven auto-layout rather than node by node is what kept it to five calls.
driftSweepProgress.redrawVerification: 25 of 25 drawn and 25 verified against a reference render (92.5-97.8%). BL-0112 was the last: it could not be verified while the Settings surface was broken, so the surface was FIXED first and a fresh reference captured. Comparison trap: a frame screenshot is NOT symmetrically padded (x is +12 per side, y about +1 at the top), so a centre-crop comparison reads ~10px low and understates agreement — crop the figma image at the target's own measured edge instead. Interpreter trap: a measured child of a plain TEXT node is positioned relative to that text, but a text node cannot hold children, so the rebuild attaches it to the text's PARENT and must add the text's own origin — BL-0112's "opens dashboard" hint landed 626px too high without it.
driftSweepProgress.harness: Two fixes on 2026-08-19 unblocked five rows that had been written off as unreachable. (1) capture.mjs and measure-region.mjs now accept a `rightClick` action — context menus need the right button, and three rows sat as "controls refuse the click from a spec" for want of it. (2) Both scripts seed the `buildrik_consent` cookie on every context instead of clicking "Essential Only" per screen: the banner covers the editor's status bar and eats clicks, and a per-screen click FAILS THE WHOLE RUN on the second screen, because the contexts are reused and there is no banner left to click.
driftSweepProgress.referenceCorpus: Checked, not assumed (2026-08-19): the site name was read off the topbar of all 49 editor references by cropping x74-240,y16-40 and comparing. 48 are the seed fixture ("E2E Blank Full d013128c"). Exactly ONE is not — BL-0171, whose topbar reads "Demo AI Site"; comparing a seed-fixture render against it read ~81% for no reason but the canvas content, and it has been recaptured on the fixture as `brand-starter-themes__seed.png`. Five rows (BL-0106, 0111, 0112, 0121, 0175) look different at first and are not: a modal scrim dims the topbar, and they match the seed template exactly once brightness is normalised. So the corpus IS uniform, with one row's worth of exception — but read the site name off a reference before believing a drift number, because nothing else in the pipeline records which site a render came from.

REDRAWN 2026-08-19 and now VERIFIED — 97.76% pixel agreement, the highest in the redraw set. The earlier note on this row said the Settings surface never paints and called that a product defect. It WAS one, and it is fixed: PanelFrame's default `narrow` width carries `tw:flex-none`, and Settings' host `.ls-fullpage-container` is a flex column, so the root resolved to its header height and every screen under it measured 1379 wide by 0 tall. `width="fullpage"` (the variant PanelFrame already shipped for this host) fixes it; a second, hidden SettingsTab that the retired drawer route still mounted was removed with it. So the reference render this row was pinned to — an empty page under a Settings header — was a picture of the bug, not of the design. A fresh reference was captured after the fix as `sitemenu-site-settings__fixed.png`; the pinned one is kept untouched. What is drawn: the whole content band (rail + full-page surface, 1440x764), replacing the old 380px drawer node 77:55, placed at frame y=104 so its bottom meets the status bar. The 48px gap above it is the ReviewBar row this frame's shell predates — the known-stale shell band, declared, not drawn.
